name: Crowd renderer: thousands of animated riders and animals
what: Draws thousands of animated, skinned horses and riders (or any rigged model: herds, flocks, people) in a few draw calls. Every clip is baked once into a float texture of bone matrices and instances are skinned in the vertex shader (24 floats per instance, no CPU skinning), with clip cross-fades, the body bent along its path, per-instance tints, variant parts and three LODs plus a far one made at load. A rider reads its horse's saddle bone in the shader, so it never drifts off. Comes with a horse, an archer and a knight built entirely in code (no model files) and the horse movement law, so the demo army moves honestly.
use_when: the game needs hundreds or thousands of animated characters, animals or mounted riders on screen at once (armies, cavalry, herds, crowds, flocks) at 60 fps in the browser
good_for: armies and cavalry, herds of horses, cattle or deer, flocks seen from the ground, stadium or market crowds; anything rigged with a few clips that must appear by the thousand; riders on mounts that must stay in the saddle
not_for: a few hero characters seen up close (use three's normal SkinnedMesh and AnimationMixer); physics ragdolls; WebGPU projects; models with more than 4 bone influences per vertex or very many bones (the bone texture is one row per frame, 3 texels per bone)
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-crowd-renderer, then import createCrowd from vendor/meticulai-crowd-renderer/src/crowd.js and the stand-ins from src/standin.js; register a model, createSet, write instances each frame; see HOW-TO-USE.md
